steps: Pair on the ground with the avionics on and the engine off.
Turn on airplane mode, then turn Bluetooth back on: the phone's cellular radio must stay off in the air.
Disconnect AirPods, the car and any other Bluetooth audio: the last one to connect takes the input.
Hold the panel's small knob for two seconds: the Bluetooth light flashes and the panel can be found for 90 seconds.
In the iPhone's Settings, Bluetooth, pick the audio panel.

Once it's connected, if PILOT isn't already blue, press PILOT and the small knob together: PILOT turns blue and you hear "Bluetooth Recording Mode Enabled". The panel remembers it for this phone; pressing them together again turns it off.
For the radio with fewer voices, use Pilot Isolate, and take the blue music and phone off PILOT in Blue-Select.
Selected NAV and marker idents and the airplane's alerts still come through, so deselect NAV and MKR when you're not identifying.
Before relying on it, tune the ATIS with the cabin speaker off and check the words follow it.
Don't use a phone call for this: Garmin documents a call carrying only the headset microphones, and only Recording Mode sending the radio.

sources: https://static.garmin.com/pumac/190-01134-12_L.pdf (GMA 350/350c Pilot's Guide 190-01134-12 Rev. L, June 2017, pp.10-11, 15-24, 36-38; seen 2026-11-04)

The app can't see whether the mode is on, and without it Garmin documents the link only as a phone or music source whose call carries the headset mics (p.36), so the line asks for PILOT blue. It is whatever the pilot hears, so isolating the intercom (pp.19, 21) and taking music and the phone off PILOT in Blue-Select (pp.23-24) leave nearly only the radio; alerts and selected NAV and marker idents still come (alerts p.18; NAV p.15; MKR pp.16-17). No report of a phone receiving it was found, and the mode depends on the panel's software (Rev. K and L of the guide describe it), so it is checked on the ground. Garmin gives no Bluetooth name; the pattern takes the model however it is spaced or followed ("GMA350c_1234").

steps: Pair on the ground with the avionics on and the engine off.
Turn on airplane mode, then turn Bluetooth back on: the phone's cellular radio must stay off in the air.
Disconnect AirPods, the car and any other Bluetooth audio: the last one to connect takes the input.

While the panel starts up, hold the lower line-select button to open the setup. Go to More, Bluetooth, BT 2 Config and set the BT2 function to Streamer, then turn the panel off and on to leave the setup.

Pair from Radio-ICS, More, Streamer, Config, Pair (Init Pair on older units), then pick the panel's BT2 in the iPhone's Settings, Bluetooth: BT2 and four digits, or 450A BT2 on a PMA450A. BT1 is off while it pairs.
If it hasn't paired in about a minute, press Cancel, wait 2 seconds and press Pair again.
Each flight, check Radio-ICS, More, Streamer, Source reads Radio, not Headphone or Off (the middle button steps through them).
On a PMA450A, and on a PMA450B whose manual says so, the Streamer is off at every power-up: turn it on each flight.
Before relying on it, tune the ATIS with the cabin speaker off and check the words follow it.
